items.title: NeurIPS apologizes after China boycotts over sanctions ban

featured_image.name: China boycotts top AI conference after ban on papers from US-sanctioned entities

items.description:
China's largest science and technology organizations announced a boycott of NeurIPS, one of the world's most prestigious artificial intelligence conferences, after it barred submissions from entities on U.S. sanctions lists — a move that effectively locked out major Chinese tech firms including Huawei and SMIC. By Friday, NeurIPS organizers issued an apology, acknowledging they had overstepped their legal obligations.

The China Association for Science and Technology (CAST) said on Friday that it would immediately stop accepting funding applications from members seeking to attend NeurIPS and would redirect researchers toward domestic conferences or "international conferences that respect the rights and interests of Chinese academics," according to Reuters. Papers published at NeurIPS will no longer qualify as research outputs for CAST's funding programs.[1][2]

items.title: Wikipedia bans AI-generated articles on English site

featured_image.name: Wikipedia votes to ban AI-generated article content

items.description: English Wikipedia has officially prohibited the use of large language models to write or rewrite articles, a policy adopted on March 20 after volunteer editors voted overwhelmingly in favor of the restriction. The new guideline, which now appears on Wikipedia's content policy pages, states that "text generated by large language models often violates several of Wikipedia's core content policies" and that their use for generating or rewriting article content "is prohibited."[1]

items.title: Iran halts two Chinese ships near Hormuz in rare reversal

featured_image.name: Gulf liner trades seize up as carriers retreat from Hormuz ...

items.description:
Two ultra-large container ships operated by China's state-owned COSCO Shipping attempted to exit the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz on Friday but abruptly reversed course near Iran's Larak Island, according to ship-tracking data and crew members stationed nearby.[1][2]

The vessels — the CSCL Indian Ocean and the CSCL Arctic Ocean, each capable of carrying 19,000 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo — executed U-turns at approximately 03:20 and 03:50 UTC, roughly 20 miles from the southern Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. The incident marked the first attempted crossing of the strait by a major container carrier since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28.[2][3][4][1]

items.title: China launches two trade barrier probes against U.S.

featured_image.name: China says it has met US trade obligations, warns against more tariffs

items.description: China's Ministry of Commerce on Friday announced two trade barrier investigations targeting the United States, directly mirroring Washington's own Section 301 probes launched earlier this month and marking a sharp escalation in the trade friction between the world's two largest economies.

items.title: Deployed nuclear warheads rose again in 2025, report finds

featured_image.name: Russia voices concern over new US submarine-launched nuclear weapon

items.description:
The number of nuclear weapons deployed and ready for use grew again in 2025, according to the annual Nuclear Weapons Ban Monitor released on March 26, underscoring what arms control experts called a dangerous trajectory at a time when the last remaining treaty limiting the world's two largest arsenals has lapsed.

The nine nuclear-armed states — the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, France, China, India, Pakistan, North Korea, and Israel — possessed a combined 12,187 warheads at the start of 2026, with 9,745 of those available for military use, an increase of 141 from the previous year. Of that total, 4,012 warheads were deployed on ballistic missiles, submarines, or at bomber bases, a rise of 108 over 2024.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio presses G7 allies on Iran as Europeans hold firm on Ukraine

featured_image.name: In France, Rubio tries to sell Iran war to skeptical G7 ...

items.description: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven nations gathered at the Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay near Paris this week for two days of talks that laid bare a widening transatlantic divide, with the United States pushing its allies to back the war against Iran while European partners insisted on sustaining military support for Ukraine and tightening sanctions on Russia.

items.title: Ukraine, Saudi Arabia sign defense deal during Zelensky's surprise visit

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy flew to Saudi Arabia to negotiate military cooperation

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday and signed a defense cooperation agreement with the kingdom, marking a new chapter in Kyiv's efforts to trade its hard-won drone warfare expertise for the advanced weapons it needs to fend off Russia.

The deal, signed before Zelensky met with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah, lays the groundwork for future contracts, technological cooperation, and investments, according to Zelensky, who announced the agreement on social media. "Ukraine is ready for long-term and mutually beneficial cooperation," Zelensky wrote on X after meeting with Ukrainian military experts already stationed in the kingdom.[1][2][3]

items.title: SpaceX IPO sparks $15M in ticker bets before filing

featured_image.name: SpaceX weighs confidential IPO filing as soon as March

items.description: SpaceX has not yet filed its IPO paperwork, but traders and retail investors are already treating it like the market event of the decade. On prediction platform Polymarket, combined trading volume on bets related to the company's valuation, listing exchange, and ticker symbol surpassed $15.2 million as of Friday, according to Reuters. The frenzy underscores the extraordinary anticipation surrounding what could become the largest initial public offering in history.[1][2]

items.title: Scientists train to dive beneath polar ice as warming accelerates Arctic research

featured_image.name: Scientists train for polar ice diving to research warming ...

items.description: From the frozen lakes of Arctic Finland to the vast ice sheets of Antarctica, researchers are pushing into some of Earth's least explored frontiers — the hidden worlds beneath polar ice — seeking to understand how climate change is reshaping these environments and what long-buried landscapes can reveal about the planet's past.

items.title: Asia-Pacific governments rush to calm markets as Middle East war drives energy crisis

featured_image.name: Philippines declares national energy emergency as Asia risks ...

items.description:
Governments across the Asia-Pacific are rolling out emergency fiscal packages, fuel subsidies, and liquidity injections as the war between the United States and Israel against Iran continues to rattle energy markets and erode economic confidence across the region.

A Reuters factbox published Friday catalogued the widening list of interventions, from emergency bond purchases in South Korea to crude oil futures intervention being weighed by Japan, as policymakers scramble to shield their economies from the fallout of a conflict now entering its second month.[1]

items.title: Kremlin denies Putin asked oligarchs to fund Ukraine war costs

featured_image.name: Putin asks oligarchs to donate to Russia's budget as cost of ...

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin convened a closed-door meeting with the country's wealthiest business leaders on Thursday and urged them to make direct financial contributions to the state budget, as the Kremlin struggles to sustain the mounting costs of its war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.

The appeal, first reported by the Financial Times citing three people familiar with the discussions, marks the first time Putin has personally asked Russia's oligarchs for money to support defense expenditures. The independent Russian outlet The Bell published a similar account Thursday evening, also citing unnamed sources.[1][2]

items.title: SpaceX eyes IPO filing as Shotwell lands TIME cover

featured_image.name: SpaceX's Gwynne Shotwell Aims to Put AI on the Moon - TIME

items.description:
TIME has put SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell on its latest cover, casting the longtime executive as the operational center of a company that has grown beyond rockets into satellite internet, lunar systems and, now, artificial intelligence. The profile arrives weeks after SpaceX said it had acquired xAI, Elon Musk’s AI company, in a deal reported by Reuters and CNBC at a combined $$1.25$$ trillion-dollar valuation, and as Reuters reported this week that the company is aiming to file IPO paperwork with regulators soon.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

The timing matters because the story TIME tells is not simply about a magazine cover. It is about whether Shotwell, one of the most influential executives in aerospace, can help steer a newly enlarged SpaceX through the risks of absorbing xAI while preparing for one of the most closely watched market debuts in years.[2][5][1]

items.title: Study finds cells, firms and cities all slow in adding new functions as they grow

featured_image.name: New study identifies shared mathematical principle linking how cells, companies, and cities diversify

items.description: A mystery novel and a fantasy epic may have little in common, but count the words inside them and a pattern emerges: new vocabulary appears quickly at first, then tapers off as the author reuses what has already been introduced. A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences finds that the same mathematical rule governs how living cells, corporations, government agencies, and cities grow and diversify — and the implications stretch from biology to business strategy.

items.title: ECB survey shows Iran war upended eurozone inflation outlook

featured_image.name: ECB still set to hold interest rates through 2026, most economists say:  Reuters poll | Reuters

items.description: Consumer confidence across Europe and the United Kingdom has deteriorated sharply as the war in Iran sends energy prices higher and revives memories of the 2022 cost-of-living crisis, according to a wave of surveys released this week.

items.title: TUM team finds fix for perovskite solar cell weathering

featured_image.name: Making perovskite solar cells finally weather-resistant and suitable for  practical use - TUM

items.description: A wave of new research from labs across Europe and Asia is tackling the biggest obstacle standing between perovskite solar cells and widespread commercial adoption: their tendency to degrade under real-world weather conditions. In parallel, new manufacturing ventures are pushing to slash production costs, bringing the next generation of solar technology closer to rooftops and industrial surfaces worldwide.

items.title: China boycotts top AI conference over US sanctions ban

featured_image.name: China boycotts top AI conference after ban on papers from US-sanctioned  entities | Reuters

items.description:
China's leading science organizations have announced a boycott of the world's premier artificial intelligence conference after it barred submissions from US-sanctioned entities, marking a sharp escalation in the technological rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

The China Association for Science and Technology (CAST), the country's largest federation for science and technology professionals, said on Friday that it would stop accepting funding applications for members wanting to attend the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, known as NeurIPS, and would redirect researchers to domestic conferences or "international conferences that respect the rights and interests of Chinese academics," according to Reuters.[1]

items.title: NASA satellite reveals hidden origins of 2025 Kamchatka tsunami

featured_image.name: SWOT satellite reveals hidden tsunami signals linked to near ...

items.description: A study published Thursday in the journal Science shows that NASA's SWOT satellite captured never-before-seen details of the tsunami spawned by the massive magnitude 8.8 earthquake off Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula last July, revealing that the event originated from a shallow rupture less than 10 kilometers beneath the ocean trench — an insight impossible to obtain from land-based instruments or seafloor sensors alone.[1][2]

items.title: FAO warns Hormuz fertilizer crisis threatens global food security

featured_image.name: Fertiliser Vessels Navigate Strait of Hormuz | Kpler Fertiliser loadings  persist as vessels look to navigate the Strait of Hormuz | Kpler - Mar 11,  2026

items.description: Farmers around the world are confronting a deepening fertilizer crisis as the war in Iran chokes off shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway that handles nearly a third of global fertilizer trade. The disruption, now entering its fourth week, is driving up food prices and threatening planting seasons from the American Midwest to sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Iran war chokes global fertilizer supply as planting season begins

featured_image.name: Fertilizer prices surge amid Iran war, sparking food security warnings

items.description: Nearly a month into the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran, the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz is choking off roughly one-third of the world's seaborne fertilizer trade, sending prices surging and raising alarms about a looming food crisis just as the Northern Hemisphere's planting season begins.[1][2]

items.title: Iran claims 1 million fighters ready for US ground invasion

featured_image.name: Inside the Basij, Iran's Militia Serving the Islamic Regime

items.description: Iran's state-run media declared Thursday that more than one million fighters have been organized for ground combat against American forces, as speculation intensifies over a potential US assault on Iran's southern coast and the strategically vital Kharg Island. The claim, reported by the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim News Agency, came alongside a warning that any US attempt to seize the Strait of Hormuz would amount to "suicide."[1][2]
